title.narrative: Asian elephant conservation education through the Kouprey Express, Cambodia.

description.narrative: The purpose of this project is to continue to fund the only environmental education team in Cambodia, and brings the plight of the Asian elephant and ivory trade to the Cambodian public. The project has expanded its reach and scope via a MoU with the Government of Cambodia to include national schools and communities in Phnom Penh and Preah Sihanouk, home to Cambodias largest port. The Kouprey Express Environmental Education Program (KE) consists of a curriculum that builds the capacities of students and teachers through a national awareness campaign that highlights poaching, wildlife trade, habitat loss and habitat degradation and fragmentation. A strong anti-ivory message aims to reduce local and regional demand and complicity in the transport of ivory into, through, and out of Cambodia. Specific project activities will include: 1) delivery of education curriculum to rural schools in the Cardamom Mountains, Kompong Som and Phnom Penh, focusing on threats to flagship species; 2) improving the understanding of key environmental issues among teachers, community educators, and leaders through training, staff development, monitoring and evaluation, and provide multiple-use long lasting educational materials; 3) conduct field trips to Phnom Tamao Wildlife Rescue Center for students and community members; 4) conducting 15+ interactive hands-on Community Night Shows; 5) conduct anti-ivory and wildlife ID trainings with Customs and Excise officers at primary points of entry; 6) raise awareness on the devastating effects of the illegal wildlife trade with a focus on elephants and ivory through community outreach programs, installation of billboards, and posting hotline stickers on 10 tuk-tuks in Phnom Penh, promoting Wildlife Alliances 24-hour nationwide wildlife crime hotline.
